Describe and check the supplied original record, not the answer to a lawsuit. A party claim, a prior finding and an open legal question are distinct recordable contents. Reporting a prior finding does not endorse it. Do not require the hidden target outcome to describe visible proceedings. No target question, proposed legal conclusion or executable law is authority for this stage. All readings remain fallible model assessments; never invent a missing identity or acceptance.
Independently read CASE originals and assess each exact source record. Review the statement's speaker, content, status, actors, property, event, date role and procedural location together. The proposed source record is fallible. Select witnesses supporting every substantive field; reject disagreement and leave insufficient context unresolved. ACCEPT means faithful source description, never acceptance of its merits or legal effect. Do not test the claim against success of the lawsuit. An accurately reported party argument remains a party argument. An unnamed lower court may be identified by its source-local role; never replace it with a guessed named court. Return observed owner/status/content_role, exact object hash and a reason. Do not repair the candidate while reviewing it. Compare each candidate against the candidate-blind original reading as well as the originals. For each field select AGREES, CONTRADICTS, or NOT_COVERED; do not silently reconcile conflicting readings. When identifying a problem, give the field, exact counter-witnesses, and the conflict, rather than repeating the candidate's explanation. ACCEPT with a contradiction is invalid. A missing actor identity must be reported, not replaced by an unrelated registered person. A source-local unnamed role is valid. Readings are not a gold answer.

The judgment of the Court was delivered by MUKHERJEA J.--This appeal is on behalf of the judgment- debtor in a proceeding for execution of a money decree and it is directed against the judgment of a Letters Patent Bench of the Punjab High Court dated 18th of May, 1949. by which the learned Judges 546 affirmed, in appeal, a decision of a single Judge of that court dated 29th October, 1946."}]},"S4e66d246790f":{"original_id":"IKWEB-1252014:L161","domain":"CASE","locator":"IKWEB-1252014:L161","origin_group":"1252014","span":[0,425],"parent_id":"S4e66d246790f","document_id":"IKWEB-1252014","passages":[{"span_id":"W2dff9f6b8605","start":0,"end":425,"text":"The original order against which the appeal was taken to the High Court was made by the Senior Subordinate Judge, Ambala, in Execution Case No. 18 of 1945 dismissing the objections preferred by the appel- lants under section 47 of the Civil Procedure Code. To appreciate the contentions that have been raised in this appeal, it would be necessary to give a short narrative of the material events in their chronological order."}]},"S1b5d070c6f58":{"original_id":"IKWEB-1252014:L162","domain":"CASE","locator":"IKWEB-1252014:L162","origin_group":"1252014","span":[0,399],"parent_id":"S1b5d070c6f58","document_id":"IKWEB-1252014","passages":[{"span_id":"W21c30eba4ee2","start":0,"end":399,"text":"On September 30, 1925, Baldev Das, the father of the appel- lants, who was, at that time the manager of a joint Hindu family, consisting of himself and his sons, executed a mortgage bond in favour of Mst. Naraini, the original-re- spondent No. 1, and another person named Talok Chand, by which certain movable properties belonging to the joint family were hypothecated to secure a loan of Rs 16,000."}]},"S29c47135bf1b":{"original_id":"IKWEB-1252014:L163","domain":"CASE","locator":"IKWEB-1252014:L163","origin_group":"1252014","span":[0,490],"parent_id":"S29c47135bf1b","document_id":"IKWEB-1252014","passages":[{"span_id":"W17b9af76dbe8","start":0,"end":490,"text":"On April 16, 1928, the appellants along with a minor brother of theirs named Sumer Chand filed a suit:--being Suit No. 23 of 1928 in the Court of the Subordinate Judge of Shahjahanpur against their father Baldev Das for partition of the joint family properties. The suit culminated in a final decree for partition on 20th July, 1928, and the joint family properties were divided by metes and bounds and separate possession was taken by the father and the sons. On 29th September, 1934, Mst."}]},"Sa38d8918c9ac":{"original_id":"IKWEB-1252014:L164","domain":"CASE","locator":"IKWEB-1252014:L164","origin_group":"1252014","span":[0,401],"parent_id":"Sa38d8918c9ac","document_id":"IKWEB-1252014","passages":[{"span_id":"W688442941677","start":0,"end":401,"text":"Naraini filed a suit in the Court of the Senior Subordinate Judge, Ambala, against Baldev Das for recovery of a sum of Rs. 12;500 only on the basis of the mortgage bond referred to above. It was stated in the plaint that the money was borrowed by the defendant as manager of a joint Hindu family and the plaintiff prayed for a decree against the mortgaged property as well as against the joint family."}]},"Sda84b44fc34d":{"original_id":"IKWEB-1252014:L165","domain":"CASE","locator":"IKWEB-1252014:L165","origin_group":"1252014","span":[0,301],"parent_id":"Sda84b44fc34d","document_id":"IKWEB-1252014","passages":[{"span_id":"Wcb1a539fc1d5","start":0,"end":301,"text":"On 18th December, 1934, the appellants made an application before the Subordinate Judge under Order I, Rule 10, and Order XXXIV, Rule 1, Civil Procedure Code, praying that they might be added as parties defendants to the suit and the points in issue arising therein might be decided in their presence."}]},"S764c24b293df":{"original_id":"IKWEB-1252014:L166","domain":"CASE","locator":"IKWEB-1252014:L166","origin_group":"1252014","span":[0,301],"parent_id":"S764c24b293df","document_id":"IKWEB-1252014","passages":[{"span_id":"Wfe87e2524db7","start":0,"end":301,"text":"It was asserted in the 547 petition that Baldev Das was not the manager of a joint family and that the family properties had been partitioned by a decree of the court, as a result of which the proper- ties alleged to be the subject-matter of the mortgage were allotted to the share of the petitioners."}]},"Sc4986463e975":{"original_id":"IKWEB-1252014:L167","domain":"CASE","locator":"IKWEB-1252014:L167","origin_group":"1252014","span":[0,397],"parent_id":"Sc4986463e975","document_id":"IKWEB-1252014","passages":[{"span_id":"Wbf1e656cd798","start":0,"end":397,"text":"In reply to this petition, the plaintiff's counsel stated in court on 7th February, 1935, that his client would give up the claim for a mortgage decree against the properties in suit and would be satisfied only with a money decree against Baldev Das personally. The plaint was amended accordingly, deleting all reference to the joint family and abandoning the claim against the mortgaged property."}]},"Sad53ad8225a2":{"original_id":"IKWEB-1252014:L168","domain":"CASE","locator":"IKWEB-1252014:L168","origin_group":"1252014","span":[0,383],"parent_id":"Sad53ad8225a2","document_id":"IKWEB-1252014","passages":[{"span_id":"W2927255f2278","start":0,"end":383,"text":"Upon this the appellants withdrew their application for being made parties to the suit and reserved their right to take proper legal action if and when necessary. On April 17, 1935, Baldev Das died and on 2nd September following the appellants as well as their mother, who figures as respondent No. 5 in this appeal, were brought on the record as legal representatives of Baldev Das."}]},"Sf7cdab5aa0ca":{"original_id":"IKWEB-1252014:L169","domain":"CASE","locator":"IKWEB-1252014:L169","origin_group":"1252014","span":[0,414],"parent_id":"Sf7cdab5aa0ca","document_id":"IKWEB-1252014","passages":[{"span_id":"W68de7d943528","start":0,"end":414,"text":"On October 9, 1935, the appellants filed a written statement in which a number of pleas were taken in answer to the plaintiff's claim and it was asserted in paragraph 10 of the written statement that Baldev Das dealt Badri or specu- lative transactions, and if any money was due to the plain- tiff at all in connection with such transactions the debt was illegal and immoral and not binding on the family property."}]},"S9f014ca2f861":{"original_id":"IKWEB-1252014:L170","domain":"CASE","locator":"IKWEB-1252014:L170","origin_group":"1252014","span":[0,490],"parent_id":"S9f014ca2f861","document_id":"IKWEB-1252014","passages":[{"span_id":"W4d8eff619d23","start":0,"end":490,"text":"On the same day the court recorded an order to the effect that as the plaintiff had given up her claim for a mortgage decree, the legal representatives of the deceased could not be allowed to raise pleas relating to the validity or otherwise of the mortgage. On 20th November, 1935, the parties arrived at a compromise and on the basis of the same, a simple money decree was passed in favour of the plaintiff for the full amount claimed in the suit together with half costs amounting to Rs."}]},"S3dc313ddd1ca":{"original_id":"IKWEB-1252014:L171","domain":"CASE","locator":"IKWEB-1252014:L171","origin_group":"1252014","span":[0,92],"parent_id":"S3dc313ddd1ca","document_id":"IKWEB-1252014","passages":[{"span_id":"W2383fab2f6d3","start":0,"end":92,"text":"425 annas odd against the estates of Baldev Das in the hands of his legal representa- tives."}]},"S7d30876f6b68":{"original_id":"IKWEB-1252014:L172","domain":"CASE","locator":"IKWEB-1252014:L172","origin_group":"1252014","span":[0,454],"parent_id":"S7d30876f6b68","document_id":"IKWEB-1252014","passages":[{"span_id":"Wb377661dbe31","start":0,"end":454,"text":"After Subordinate Judge, Ambala, and in accordance with the prayer contained therein, the court directed the attachment of certain immovable properties consisting of a number of shops in possession of the appellants and situated at a place called Abdullaput."}]},"S65959eb57e13":{"original_id":"IKWEB-1252014:L173","domain":"CASE","locator":"IKWEB-1252014:L173","origin_group":"1252014","span":[0,370],"parent_id":"S65959eb57e13","document_id":"IKWEB-1252014","passages":[{"span_id":"W44c8bd95b087","start":0,"end":370,"text":"On belong to Baldev Das but were the separate and exclusive properties of the objectors which they obtained on partition with their father long before the decree was passed."}]},"S487ef87e25a2":{"original_id":"IKWEB-1252014:L174","domain":"CASE","locator":"IKWEB-1252014:L174","origin_group":"1252014","span":[0,204],"parent_id":"S487ef87e25a2","document_id":"IKWEB-1252014","passages":[{"span_id":"Wead2262b1c19","start":0,"end":204,"text":"It was asserted that these properties could not be made liable for the satisfac- tion of the decretal dues which had to be realised under the terms of the decree itself from the estate left by Baldev Das."}]},"Sb842c2dece3b":{"original_id":"IKWEB-1252014:L175","domain":"CASE","locator":"IKWEB-1252014:L175","origin_group":"1252014","span":[0,477],"parent_id":"Sb842c2dece3b","document_id":"IKWEB-1252014","passages":[{"span_id":"W3e958af361cb","start":0,"end":477,"text":"After hearing the parties and the evidence adduced by them the Subordinate Judge came to the conclusion that there was in fact a partition between Baldev Das and his sons in the year 1928 and as a result of the same, the properties, which were attached at the instance of the decree holder, were allotted to the share of the sons. The decree sought to be executed was obtained after the partition, but it was in respect of a debt which was contracted by the father prior to it."}]},"S7861a3aa3085":{"original_id":"IKWEB-1252014:L176","domain":"CASE","locator":"IKWEB-1252014:L176","origin_group":"1252014","span":[0,325],"parent_id":"S7861a3aa3085","document_id":"IKWEB-1252014","passages":[{"span_id":"We9fcecb1fc58","start":0,"end":325,"text":"It was held in these circumstances that the separate share of the sons which they obtained on partition was liable under the Hindu law for the pre-partition debt of their father if it was not immoral and under section 53 of the Civil Procedure Code the decreeholder was entitled to execute the decree against such properties."}]},"Sc8d43e93b852":{"original_id":"IKWEB-1252014:L177","domain":"CASE","locator":"IKWEB-1252014:L177","origin_group":"1252014","span":[0,414],"parent_id":"Sc8d43e93b852","document_id":"IKWEB-1252014","passages":[{"span_id":"W6963edae5f5c","start":0,"end":414,"text":"As no point was raised by the objectors in their petition alleging that the debt covered by the decree was tainted with immorality, the objections under section 47, Civil Procedure Code, were dismissed.
